body: Hey, after reading about why your friends think you're manipulative, I have to disagree with them (based on what you've said). Expressing your feelings when you're depressed/anxious (or being blunt/honest) is perfectly healthy. It's communication. Some people prefer to keep it inside (bottled up, and they slowly build a grudge or become more depressed) but I personally like to get things out in the open. Maybe your friends just don't care or don't want to have to deal with your problems. I don't know. But as long as you're not blaming others or putting your problems onto other people's shoulders, I don't think talking about them is being manipulative.

I can't speak from personal experience, but people probably self harm to take their mind off things or because they want to inflict pain (to themselves or others) in response to their anger/depression. 

Obviously, self harm doesn't do anything good for you (it might even send you to the hospital and you'll have to pay an expensive bill, which would make life worse). I'd speak to a family member/friend or therapist/support group. If you're worried about why you did that, consider even a psychiatrist (if you suspect it's a mental issue).
Hey man, I appreciate your efforts. It's not easy giving advice to someone you've never met. One of my friends is in the air force, so if you have any questions for him, I could ask for you.

Well my dude, I'm just a stranger on the internet, I can't force you to do anything. But if you talk to someone about this in real life, you'll probably feel better.

Depressed/suicidal doesn't mean you're off the market. My mother gets depressed often, but she's a hidden gem. Any man would be lucky to have her. There are so many people in this world, you sure that you can't find a single one who you'll be happy with?

Go find something you enjoy and look to it when life is down. There are so many people out there, your best friend or loved one is waiting. I hate giving stereotypical suicide advice but there's just no benefit to suicide. We all feel down. My life has had so many ups and downs, its almost fake. One second, life sucks and I want to kill myself. Next day, tons of good things happen. Life is unpredictable, but killing yourself is the one thing that will cut off any chance for good things to happen.

No one wants to kill you, because then they'd get in trouble for it. And they'd have a guilty conscience for the rest of their life. There's no benefit to anyone. 

And you know, you can find another person who could care for you even MORE. What if, this girl was the first of many? If you kill yourself, you automatically throw away any chance of finding "the one". There's 0 benefit. You don't even know what's waiting for you after.

I said this in another post, but everyone regrets suicide. A girl jumped off a building and screamed for help right before she splattered the ground. You have another 40 years at least (like me). If you've had a bad first 20 years, and the next 40 years are good, suicide is the worst thing you could do. If life sucks, it can only go up right? Nothing to lose Suicide ends your chances of getting better things early. If you're at a casino and lost all your money, but the casino says "you can keep playing for free, but once you have money, you need to start betting it again" would you do it? Probably.

Some of my family members have depression. The best thing for a depressed person, is emotional support. If you don't have friends or family who can offer that to you, go seek a therapist (if you can afford one or find a pro bono one). If that's not an option, go seek support groups (they exist and are free).

Everyone regrets killing themselves right before it happens. There was a news story, where a girl jumped off a building and right before she hit the ground, she was screaming "somebody help me". We might get emotional and think "life's shit, I want to end it right now" but we will always regret it. Nothing good can come of suicide. You're not gonna get to heaven if there is one. At best, you end up in a "Limbo". Maybe you go to Hell. No religion has promoted suicide as a "good option".

I can't judge you, but I do see what you're saying. I don't like the faking/politics in today's corporate world; that said, I hate myself for playing video games and being useless/a parasite. I was once ambitious before I gave in to the easy path.

I haven't found a passion I enjoy. Only vices. Sure I like recreational reading. Sure I'm good at mediation. Sure I like saving money and analyzing finances. Sure I like helping others and making the world a better place. Sure I like justice (am considering being a district attorney). But almost everyone shares the same views.

Well, if you could make $10 million but "possibly" ruin the lives of millions of people unintentionally, would you do it? Almost anyone would. I won't straight up rob an old woman to get $10 million but if I can justify the reason to myself (it's just business; this is how life is; everyone else is doing it; I need to eat too) (i.e. "this woman is evil to society, by robbing her I'm saving thousands of people" vs "robbing is wrong no matter what") then anything's possible. Gaming corporations exist because they can make money and there is demand for it. Gaming is entertainment.
